context.body: The bounded canonical source is Deuteronomy 7:6–11; its local speaker, audience, sequence, and literary form remain controlling evidence.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Israel is called holy and treasured, but election is explicitly denied a basis in size.
observations.label: Israel is chosen despite being few: action

observations.body: love, oath, deliverance, covenant faithfulness, and judgment frame the choice.
observations.label: Israel is chosen despite being few: response

payload.posture: Read Deuteronomy 7:6–11 as identity before the land evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The passage grounds choice in divine love and promise without explaining why love fell on Israel rather than another people.
payload.title: Israel is chosen despite being few
